sample.name: Spruce Hill Bird Sanctuary
facts: The Spruce Hill Community Association bought the lot in 1981.
Landscape architects Julie Bush and Ann Froehling designed the layout in 2011.
A Dept of Agriculture grant helped turn the lot into the sanctuary.

sample.name: Cadwalader Tract
facts: Listed by Haverford Township among its parks as a designated nature area.

sample.name: 48th & Woodland Playground
facts: Its sprayground reopened after upgrades in July 2024.
The sprayground was redesigned around a learning theme.

sample.name: Fitler Square
facts: Created from a former brickyard by city ordinance in 1896.
Named for Edwin H. Fitler, Philadelphia mayor from 1887 to 1891.
Half-acre park maintained with the Fitler Square Improvement Association.

sample.name: Grays Ferry Crescent Trail Park
facts: The park is a former industrial site turned riverfront park and trail on the Schuylkill River.
Groundbreaking took place in 2009 after a capital campaign.

sample.name: Wynnewood Valley Park: Garden for the Blind
facts: The Ardmore Rotary Club built and dedicated the garden in 1977.
Reconstruction began in 2010, and the restored garden was rededicated on May 9, 2011.

sample.name: Camden Children's Garden
facts: Horticultural playground for children and families that opened in July 1999.
Includes the Philadelphia Eagles Four Seasons Butterfly House and a Dinosaur Garden, Maze and Tree House.
Also has a carousel and a train ride.

sample.name: West Wayne Preserve
facts: The preserve is part of a wooded wetlands restoration and habitat enhancement project.

sample.name: Fernhill Park
facts: Community food forest started here in fall 2021 with the Philadelphia Orchard Project.
The 51-acre park in southwest Germantown has trees, sports courts and playgrounds.

sample.name: Aubrey Collins Park
facts: Reopened after renovation on October 10, 2020.
Rededicated as Aubrey Collins Jr. Park.

sample.name: Mary Wood Park
facts: Mary Wood left the block to the borough in her will in 1919 for use as a public park.
Her house became the borough community center, formed in 1925.

sample.name: Shofuso Japanese House and Garden
facts: Designed by Junzō Yoshimura

sample.name: Bocce Grove
facts: Run by Tredyffrin Township

sample.name: Henry Lane Park
facts: Covers 22.0 acres in Gladwyne.
Nature park with hiking and bridle trails.
Run by Lower Merion Township

sample.name: Cloverly Park
facts: Two-acre passive park on land the Edward White Clark family donated to the city in 1914.
Friends of Cloverly Park, an all-volunteer group, has cared for the park since 1986.

sample.name: Gorgas Park
facts: Gorgas Park covers 20 acres along 6300 Ridge Avenue.
The park was dedicated on July 4, 1893 by the city of Philadelphia.
Friends of Gorgas Park was established in 1997 to restore the park.

sample.name: Merwood Park
facts: Neighborhood park of about 5.8 acres in Haverford Township.
Has a ball field, basketball courts and a reservable picnic pavilion.

sample.name: Westover Park
facts: Run by Tredyffrin Township

sample.name: Sharpe Park Bird Sanctuary
facts: Sharpe Park and Bird Sanctuary covers 2.3 acres at West Montgomery Avenue and Haverford Station Road.
The township classes it as a nature park and bird sanctuary, and leashed dogs are permitted.
Run by Lower Merion Township

sample.name: Penn Park
facts: Penn Park is a 24-acre park on the University of Pennsylvania campus beside the Schuylkill River.
Penn Park was completed in September 2011 and has two athletic fields, a tennis center and picnic areas.
Penn Park Orchard was started in fall 2014 with the Philadelphia Orchard Project.

sample.name: Mom Rinker's Rock
facts: Scenic outlook on a ridge in Wissahickon Valley Park, just north of the Walnut Lane Bridge.
Named for Molly Rinker, said to have watched British troop movements from the rock in the Revolutionary War.

sample.name: Clarence H. Clark Park
facts: Clark Park covers 9.1 acres between 43rd and 45th streets and Baltimore and Woodland Avenues.
The park was established in 1895 on land donated by banker Clarence Howard Clark.
It holds a life-sized 1890 sculpture of Charles Dickens.

sample.name: Washington Square
facts: Originally laid out as Southeast Square, one of five squares in William Penn's plan for Philadelphia.
The square was planned by William Penn's surveyor Thomas Holme.
The park covers about 6.4 acres in Center City.

sample.name: Gest Tract Park
facts: Neighborhood park of about 20 acres in Haverford Township, Delaware County.
Has swing sets and walking paths.

sample.name: Highland Farms Park
facts: Has tennis and pickleball courts and a playground.
Used as an activity location in the township's summer recreation programs.
